question: Shared once P-203 is read correctly: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion among ADNI MCI participants, with structural MRI as a shared channel. The ledger's P-203 figure (91.1%) is its AD vs CN accuracy, so the pair is judged on P-203's printed conversion accuracy (condition 6). P-203 (Chen et al., Front Aging Neurosci 2022) classifies pMCI (conversion within 0-36 months) vs sMCI (stable 0-90 months) from whole-brain T1 images, trained on ADNI-1 and tested on ADNI-2 (75 pMCI / 241 sMCI). P-212 (Rye et al., Sci Rep 2022) classifies MCI converting to probable AD at any later visit vs MCI stable at all visits (at least 3 visits), from demographics, neuropsychological tests, FreeSurfer total hippocampal volume and APOE, with an internal 79/21 split (test 65 converters / 74 stable). Horizon, predictor set (one MRI scalar plus cognition vs whole images), cohort phases and validation differ; condition 1 allows these.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (P-212 prints no AUC). Both papers also print sensitivity and specificity, which are the accuracies within the converter and stable subsets.

figures.P-203: ADNI-1 -> ADNI-2 test, 316 MCI (75 pMCI / 241 sMCI): accuracy 0.801, no interval printed. Wilson on n = 316: centre (0.801 + 1.9208/316)/(1 + 3.8416/316) = 0.797, half-width 0.044, CI [0.754, 0.841]. Printed sensitivity 0.520 (39/75, Wilson [0.409, 0.629]) and specificity 0.856 (206/241, Wilson [0.805, 0.894]) give (39 + 206)/316 = 0.775 (Wilson [0.726, 0.818]), not the printed 0.801. Majority-class rate 241/316 = 0.763; balanced accuracy (0.520 + 0.856)/2 = 0.688. AUC 0.789 (Hanley-McNeil with 75/241: SE 0.0332, CI [0.724, 0.854]).
figures.P-212: Held-out test set of 139 (65 cAD / 74 sMCI). Random forest 92/139 = 0.662, Wilson [0.580, 0.735]; ensemble 95/139 = 0.683, Wilson [0.602, 0.755]. Mean accuracy over 50 CV folds on the 539 training subjects 74.6% (RF) and 74.9% (ensemble); Wilson for 0.749 at n = 539: [0.711, 0.784]. RF sensitivity 40/65 = 0.615 [0.494, 0.724], specificity 52/74 = 0.703 [0.591, 0.795]; ensemble sensitivity 41/65 = 0.631 [0.509, 0.738], specificity 54/74 = 0.730 [0.619, 0.818]. Balanced accuracy 0.659 (RF) and 0.680 (ensemble); majority-class rate 74/139 = 0.532.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports the other's input, horizon or cohort. The only common-condition figures are the per-class accuracies, that is, results in the same population subset. In the converter subset the papers agree: P-203's sensitivity 0.520 [0.409, 0.629] and P-212's 0.615-0.631 (intervals from 0.494-0.509 to 0.724-0.738) lie inside each other's intervals. In the stable subset they do not: P-203's specificity 0.856 [0.805, 0.894] against 0.703-0.730 (upper bounds 0.795-0.818). Weighting the two subsets equally, the balanced accuracies are 0.688 and 0.659-0.680. P-203's own sensitivity and specificity at P-212's test class mix give 0.520*65/139 + 0.856*74/139 = 0.699, inside both P-212 test intervals. The headline gap therefore tracks the converter share of the test sets (24% vs 47%) and a threshold in P-203 that favours specificity. Whether these per-class figures count as a matched figure that dissolves the gap is the open point.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the exclusion: no accuracy or AUC reaches 0.97 (P-203 0.801 / 0.789; P-212 at most 0.749). P-203's test is a cross-phase ADNI-1 -> ADNI-2 evaluation; P-212 uses an internal held-out set.

candidate_explanations.difference: Class balance of the evaluation sets: 24% converters in P-203's ADNI-2 test against 47% in P-212's test. Plain accuracy weights specificity more heavily in P-203; its 0.801 barely exceeds its majority-class rate (0.763), and its balanced accuracy (0.688) matches P-212's (0.659-0.680).
candidate_explanations.quote: The ADNI-2 dataset has 643 3T T1W sMR brain images, including 143 AD, 184 CN, 75 pMCI, and 241 sMCI.

candidate_explanations.difference: The same point from P-212's side: its classes are near-balanced.
candidate_explanations.quote: The other diagnostic group was defined as converters to AD (cAD; n = 321, 47.3%), and included subjects who were diagnosed with MCI at their first study visit, but met the criteria for probable AD on a subsequent assessment

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition and horizon: conversion within 36 months against stability over 0-90 months (P-203) vs conversion at any later visit against stability at all visits with at least 3 visits (P-212).
candidate_explanations.quote: Progressive MCI (pMCI): Subjects are diagnosed with MCI who would gradually progress to AD within 0–36 months.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: whole-brain T1 images through a multiview-slice attention and 3D CNN (P-203) vs neuropsychological tests, one hippocampal volume, APOE and demographics in a random forest or ensemble (P-212). The difference would lead one to expect P-212 higher, not lower.
candidate_explanations.quote: with cognitive function, hippocampal volume and genetic APOE status as features, we obtained a cross-validation classification accuracy of about 70%.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design: P-203 trains on ADNI-1 (1.5 T) and tests on ADNI-2 (3 T); P-212 uses a stratified internal split whose test accuracy (66-68%) sits below its own CV mean (about 75%).
candidate_explanations.quote: When the model was evaluated on our unseen test set, the overall classification accuracy was 66.2%.

candidate_explanations.difference: Reporting: P-203's printed accuracy (0.801) does not match its own sensitivity and specificity on its stated test set (0.775).
candidate_explanations.quote: MSA3D 0.911 0.888 0.914 0.950 0.898 0.801 0.520 0.856 0.789 0.553 (Table 4 row: AD vs CN ACC, SEN, SPE, AUC, F1; pMCI vs sMCI ACC, SEN, SPE, AUC, F1; cells joined)

reason: On the printed conversion figures the pair meets conditions 1, 2, 4 and 5: P-203's 0.801 [0.754, 0.841] and P-212's test accuracies 0.662-0.683 (upper bounds 0.735-0.755) exclude each other, and the ledger's 91.1% misreading (AD vs CN) does not create the gap. But the two accuracies come from test sets with 24% and 47% converters. In the converter subset the papers agree (sensitivity 0.52 vs 0.62), the difference sits in the stable subset, and the balanced accuracies agree (0.688 vs 0.659-0.680); P-203's printed accuracy also does not match its own sensitivity and specificity (0.775). Whether these per-class figures count as a matched figure that dissolves the gap (a condition-3 failure) is the operator's call. If they do not, the pair qualifies, with class balance as the leading candidate explanation and none shown to be sufficient.
